title: The Italian Plant-Based Board
seo_title: Vegan Italian Antipasto Board for 6–8: Shopping List
description: A vegan Italian antipasto board for 6–8: cashew mozzarella, cashew parmesan, white bean dip, caponata, artichokes, roasted peppers, olives and crostini.
hook: An Italian antipasto board with no dairy and no meat: cashew mozzarella with basil, a white bean bruschetta dip, caponata and all the jarred favorites.
why: Most of an Italian antipasto board was already plant-based: marinated artichokes, roasted peppers, olives, sun-dried tomatoes and bread. Swap the cheese for cashew mozzarella and a sprinkle of cashew parmesan and the board tastes the same.

Caponata, Sicily's sweet-and-sour eggplant relish, does what cured meat usually does here: it brings the rich, savoury bite. Spoon it onto crostini with a little white bean dip, and finish the mozzarella with basil, olive oil and flaky salt.

timeline.what: Take the cashew mozzarella out of the fridge; drain the jarred vegetables.
Fill the bowls with white bean dip, caponata and olives.
Place the mozzarella with basil and tomatoes; drizzle with oil and balsamic.
Add the artichokes, peppers and sun-dried tomatoes.
Fan the crostini and grissini; scatter cashew parmesan and sea salt.

faq.a: Yes, every item is plant-based. Check the labels on crackers, breads and store-bought dips, which sometimes contain butter, milk, honey or egg.

faq.q: What can I use instead of cashew mozzarella?
faq.a: Any fresh-style vegan mozzarella works, or use extra white bean dip seasoned with lemon, garlic and basil.

faq.q: How many people does it serve?
faq.a: 6 to 8 people as an appetizer, on a 14–18 inch board.
